channel.title: Crypto Bulletin
channel.description: Crypto Bulletin reports crypto news on bitcoin, ethereum, stablecoins, exchanges, DeFi protocols, regulation, security incidents and market structure.

item.title: RPC delays can leave swaps pending after broadcast
item.description: RPC delays can leave a swap marked pending after submission; receipts, confirmations and contract outcomes show what happened and when to act without repeating the trade.

item.title: How to Judge a Crypto Pool When Rewards End
item.description: After rewards stop, judge liquidity by trade depth, fee income and LP withdrawals across pool sizes and quiet periods; TVL and one volume spike can mislead.

item.title: How Much Slippage Should a Business Token Swap Allow?
item.description: A business should set swap slippage from its minimum acceptable proceeds, then adjust for pool depth, trade size and the cost of a failed transaction.

item.title: How Token Freeze Controls Affect Cross-Chain Deposits
item.description: Token freeze controls can pause transfers or block addresses, but a cross-chain deposit may involve separate contracts and administrators on each network.

item.title: Why Some Crypto Bridges Require a Separate Claim
item.description: A separate claim lets the destination chain verify a transfer and release funds, adding a fee and a step that some bridges remove with relayers.

item.title: Token decimals turn integer balances into readable amounts
item.description: Token decimals set how integer balances appear to users; learn the base-unit conversion, why precision matters, and what to verify before sending or integrating a token.

item.title: Cross-chain swap costs include more than the quoted fee
item.description: A cross-chain swap's real cost is the gap between what leaves your wallet and what arrives, plus source and destination gas paid separately.

item.title: Chainflip Vault Swap Approvals: How to Estimate the Amount
item.description: Estimate a Chainflip vault swap approval by comparing the token allowance for the Vault with the quoted input amount; native assets need no ERC-20 approval.

item.title: Four Steps to Set a Solana CLMM Price Range
item.description: A Solana CLMM range sets where liquidity earns fees and converts between tokens; four checks help size boundaries, understand tick limits and avoid idle capital.

item.title: Crypto treasuries should map tokens before selling
item.description: Before selling, map each token by chain, choose the asset and network you want to receive, then compare conversion, transfer, execution costs and timing.

item.title: A Missing Token May Be on Another Network or Hidden
item.description: A missing token is often present on another network or hidden from the wallet’s token list; check the transaction, chain and contract before retrying a transfer.

item.title: How to Recover a Mantle Bridge Transfer After Closing the Page
item.description: Closing Mantle’s bridge page does not erase a submitted transfer. Use the original wallet and transaction hash to check progress, then finish any withdrawal claim.

item.title: Why Bridges Need Gas on Both Chains
item.description: A bridge moves tokens across networks, but each chain charges for its own transactions. Learn when ETH is needed on both sides and how to avoid a stuck transfer.

item.title: LP token burns and reserve withdrawals change different things
item.description: Burning LP tokens can remove a claim on pooled assets, while withdrawing reserves changes the pool itself; transaction details show which event occurred.

item.title: How Much Slippage Should You Set for a BNB Smart Chain Swap?
item.description: A 0.5% starting point suits many liquid BNB Smart Chain swaps, but pool depth, price movement and token fees determine when a wider limit is justified.

item.title: How to Cancel a Pending Transaction Before Bridging
item.description: A pending wallet transaction can often be replaced before it reaches the chain; after a bridge deposit or withdrawal is confirmed, the bridge’s own process takes over.

item.title: Multisignature Bridge Withdrawals Need Two Approvals
item.description: Treasury teams can approve a Polygon PoS withdrawal in two stages, with the multisig authorizing the Polygon burn and later the Ethereum claim after checkpointing.

item.title: Polygon Bridge Transfers: From Send to Arrival
item.description: A Polygon PoS bridge deposit locks tokens on Ethereum, mints a matching balance on Polygon, and completes after the source transaction is confirmed.

item.title: When Does an Omnichain Transfer Need Destination Liquidity?
item.description: A cross-chain transfer needs destination liquidity when it must pay out or swap existing assets; mint-and-release designs can settle without a local pool.

item.title: How NFT Bridges Move a Token Between Chains
item.description: An NFT bridge locks or burns the source token, sends a verified message, then releases or mints its counterpart; metadata and provenance depend on the design.
